correctness.rationale: The matrices are row-stochastic with the asserted initial distribution and sole accepting state. Independently multiplied the full row vectors for all 27 inputs using denominator 6^4=1296. Every entry agrees with the frozen table; abc has numerator 1128, cbc has 1104, and all other words have at most 936. Thus the gap is 24/1296=1/54. A one-state stochastic matrix is [1] for every letter, so no one-state witness can give a positive gap. The result concerns the stated alphabet and the particular witness, not an optimal two-state gap. Independent replay: node /workspace/replays/5.js; the uploaded Python was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: No optimal-gap claim or classification for three-letter alphabets is verified by this computation.
